rationale.why: The interior mid-point of the 10-value hue ring. (a) It is the object's own photometric property — the thing the request names and the judge scores — unlike floor_hue/wall_hue, which are background. (b) Hue is CIRCULAR, so no hue value is a physical default the model degrades towards; the §3.1 hazard that rules out scale and orientation does not apply to it. (c) It sits four grid steps from Montero's retained band (object_hue >= 0.8), so the value hole does not sit inside the region the headline and wide COMBINATION conditions already spend. (d) It is interior, so BOTH of its grid neighbours are retained and the hole is two-sided — a hole at 0.0 or 0.9 would sit on the realised range boundary, where build_c_invalid's out_of_range records are also placed, and rows 5 and 6 would become adjacent in value space.

rationale.why: The cube is the shape most distant from the retained set under the only degradation mode we have measured. r6_invalid_refusal.why: ⛔ SANITY CHECK ONLY, and it can never be anything else: out-of-range is decidable from the factor grid alone. Kept as the degenerate-arm guard; ⛔ a row-6 number is NOT evidence that the store computes a barrier.

r7_deletion.why: ⭐ THE strongest instrument. Deleting a value from the store does not move the factor grid, so the no-model rule's delta_reject is exactly 0.0. A changed refusal after a deletion, with NO retraining, is not producible by any syntactic rule.

scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.
